difficulty.hint: A 0-1 delivery-difficulty score combining distance from warehouse, volume (raw parcel count in the queried range), and volume density (parcels/km²) — higher is harder. Shown as a Vendor → Route code → Postcode hierarchy — expand each row to drill down. Vendor difficulty is the simple (unweighted) average of its route codes' scores, not volume-weighted — one route code is roughly one driver line, and a low-volume, far, sparse route is exactly the kind that's hardest to keep a driver on, so weighting by volume would marginalize it. Postcodes missing coordinates or boundary area are excluded from scoring.
difficulty.avgVolumeHint: Avg volume = total parcels / valid days (days with 0 or under 300 arrivals are excluded automatically — {{days}} valid day(s) this range)
difficulty.avgVolumeLoading: Computing avg volume… (fetching arrivals day by day, a few seconds)

merge.noSuggestionsHint: No low-volume routes to merge right now
merge.hint: Clusters a supplier's own low-volume routes (below the threshold) that sit close together into merge suggestions — never across suppliers, since each supplier runs its own independent fleet/drivers and can't merge deliveries with another supplier's. The closest routes merge first; a group stops absorbing more routes as soon as its total volume hits the cap below — a real physical limit (what a van can carry, what a driver can finish in a day). There's no cap on profit: more profit is always better for the driver, so it's only used for ranking, never to block a merge. Ranked by combined courier profit: this answers "do these routes, each too small on their own, add up to a trip worth running" — merging itself doesn't create extra profit (courier profit is priced per parcel, independent of how many trips it takes).
merge.empty: No merge suggestions at the current thresholds — try raising the volume threshold or cluster distance
